title: Choose busbar's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Flight Strip Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. This world carries the bb ui dashboard first, then the landing/docs site and the video's faux UI.

options.label: Flight Strip Board
options.lineage: air-traffic-control flight progress strips and strip bays
options.thesis: Every value is a strip in a rack; busbar works the board and hands you the one strip it can't clear.
materials: printed strip stock in coloured holders
options.viewport: Left: a sector map, the source value (tunnel URL) at the fix with routes to Razorpay, Stripe, Meta and Google. Right: the strip bay in four bays: Plan, Active, Your turn, Cleared. The one strip cocked out of the rack is your Meta step, with its deep link.
options.risk: ATC grammar is unfamiliar to most devs, so labels must stay literal; paper texture would turn it into costume.

raised.raise: Focus a value and every unrelated route and strip dims while the selected strip lifts.
The rack is a visible grid: strips occupy whole slots and the layout reflows by whole strips, never by squishing.
Strip text sits at one size; rank comes from weight, case and reversal, never from a bigger font.
Every state carries a mark as well as a colour: stamp is verified, struck rule is drift, open box is unknown.
Each bay carries a right-aligned running count, so the size of the plan is always legible.

options.label: Interlocking Panel
options.lineage: railway NX route-setting panels and signal-box mimic diagrams
options.thesis: Set a route, the interlocking locks it, and the signal only clears when the track proves it.
options.viewport: A full-width mimic diagram: the source value enters at left, lines fan out to provider platforms, route lamps show the plan, and each destination has a signal that turns green only after verify.
options.risk: My most familiar candidate: lamp-lit diagrams drift toward the dark node-graph dashboard every dev tool already ships.

options.label: High-Density Module Grid
options.thesis: Every provider is a ruled module with a red tab; your whole stack fits on one screen.
options.viewport: A packed mosaic of provider modules, each listing its registered values, with drift badged in utility red.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: providers become modules and values become rows; dense scanning suits the task, but devs don't recognise the world.
options.risk: Cross-provider routes vanish into module borders, so busbar's one unique view is the hardest thing to see.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: Providers as rows of tiles; the focused value grows and explains itself.
options.viewport: Rows per provider, each value a tile, metadata only on focus.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hiding metadata until focus defeats scanning for drift, and devs don't browse config like films.
options.risk: Drift and verify state stay invisible until you hover.
options.kept: Focus discipline: the selected thing lifts and everything unrelated dims.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The layout grid is visible and everything snaps to its cells.
options.viewport: A visible cell grid with values snapped into cells.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a designer's world, and monumental letterforms fight a dense operations task.
options.risk: Becomes a poster about grids instead of a tool.
options.kept: The grid as a visible, literal armature that layouts reflow by.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: The plan as a tracklist timed to fit a side.
options.viewport: Plan steps as side A, verify as side B.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nostalgic and handwritten, the opposite of verified infra.
options.risk: Reads as craft-project whimsy on production config.
options.kept: Honest running totals, right-aligned tight against the margin.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1970s pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: Every value in one type size, rank by weight and reversal alone.
options.viewport: A raked rack of slides, one per provider.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the rake slows scanning and the world is unfamiliar to devs.
options.risk: Angled containers cost legibility on a task screen.
options.kept: One type size for data; rank carried by weight, case and reversal.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.lineage: printer's exposure cards and zone ramps
options.thesis: Drift drawn as hatch density, conflict as cross-hatching.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets per provider, conflicts cross-hatched.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an obscure craft world, and hatching is slower to read than marks.
options.risk: Beautiful but cryptic on a screen you open mid-build.
options.kept: State that reads without colour: every status has its own mark.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Vercel/Linear-grade dev dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, project header, a node graph of providers, and a table of values with status dots.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other dev tool by design.
